7107d0640bb166d2a3bdd83cff718455d6ffc6f5: Corvatsch offers 120 km of well-marked runs — a medium-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 14 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Corvatsch has kept an authentic mountain village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoiled landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. When it comes to snow, Corvatsch is in a strong position with its summit at 3303 m — even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well until April. The village at 1797 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from mid-December. A stay at Corvatsch is clearly a high-budget option: €89 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short, Corvatsch lives up to its promises. A resort in the Northern Alps that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.
710ae345822f5db350ef2c02979a418a48fed05b: A resort on a human scale, Kals-Matrei prioritises the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 40 km of runs are well suited to a 3–4 day stay, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly switch up their playground. Kals-Matrei's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Kals-Matrei's altitude (933 m at the bottom, 2,426 m at the top) helps it keep decent snow cover through midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Kals-Matrei is clearly high: 74€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you set off. In short: Kals-Matrei doesn't rival the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
